description: The spacing scope of Multi-brand: its answers, its usage rules and the semantic tokens it owns. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

answers.question: spacing.roles
answers.why: Account tables need a row height.

answers.question: spacing.definition
answers.why: Every brand shares one set of steps, so they sit on a 4px grid: small enough for account forms, with big ones for product pages.

answers.question: spacing.lands
answers.why: Space matters most between form fields.

usage.why: Cards hold each offer together, so customers compare offers as units in every brand. Lines would split an offer apart.
Customers browse on phones, and compact rows are hard to tap in any brand.
Parts of one item sit close in every brand, so the shared parts look the same.
Fields in a form keep a comfortable gap, so customers on phones tap the right one.
One group gap in every brand keeps sign-up forms the same shape.
Shared padding keeps buttons the same size in every brand.
Cards hold offers the same way in every brand; only the corner and color change.
Account tables keep room between columns on a phone in every brand.

open-ds.why: Every brand shares small steps on a 4px grid, so the base is 4px. Comfortable density sets each multiple, with big steps for product pages.

We use 8px for the tight gap between the parts of one item in order to group and separate: two base steps (2 × 4px) on the shared grid. Distance does this by grouping what is near and separating what is far, as the eye reads proximity (Gestalt), so a gap between groups stays clearly larger than a gap inside one. So the shared parts look the same in every brand, because the brands share one set of steps on a 4px grid (spacing.definition) and three brands share one system (business.q2).

We use 12px for the default gap between the fields of one form group in order to group and separate: three base steps (3 × 4px), one step wider than the tight gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so customers on phones tap the right field, because the layout is comfortable (spacing.values) and customers sign up on phones (scenarios.q1).

We use 24px for the group gap between groups in a form in order to group and separate: six base steps (6 × 4px), twice the default gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so sign-up forms keep the same shape in every brand, because three brands share one system (business.q2) and the layout is comfortable (spacing.values).

We use 48px for the section gap between page sections in order to group and separate: twelve base steps (12 × 4px), twice the group gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so each offer card stands apart on a product page, because the layout is comfortable (spacing.values) and the 4px grid holds big steps for product pages (spacing.definition).

We use 16px for the inline padding inside controls in order to give content room inside its box: four base steps (4 × 4px), the same as a table cell. Padding does this by keeping content off the edge of its box, so the content reads as part of that box, and by setting the size of the box with the content. So buttons are the same size in every brand, because three brands share one system (business.q2) and steps sit on a 4px grid (spacing.definition).

We use 24px for the padding inside cards and dialogs in order to give content room inside its box: six base steps (6 × 4px), the same as the group gap. Padding does this by the rule given for space.inset.control-x, so cards hold offers the same way in every brand, because three brands share one system (business.q2) and the layout is comfortable (spacing.values).

We use 16px for the inline padding inside table cells in order to give content room inside its box: four base steps (4 × 4px), the same as a control. Padding does this by the rule given for space.inset.control-x, so account tables keep room between columns on a phone, because customers sign up on phones (scenarios.q1) and the layout is comfortable (spacing.values).

We use 44px for one table row in order to keep the eye on its row: a row is one 44px default control tall, as rows stay one control tall. Row height does this by making each row a band the eye follows across, and a hit target when the row is clickable (WCAG 2.5.8: 24px). So rows stay easy to tap on a phone, and a control sits in a row with no gap, because account tables need a row height (spacing.roles) and the layout is comfortable (spacing.values).
